name: Spring dash stack, sideways: a flat spring dash carries the first spring's momentum into a second one
techNote: The sideways case of spring-dash-stack. A floor (top y 0, x -300-100) and two springs pointing right (the Course 5 ceiling spring's SpringScript: upForce 70, strength 300, movementLock 0.25; triggers 80x80 at x 60-140 and x 360-440, y 0-80, turned -90 so transform.up is (1, 0)); a spike strip (x 150-4450, y -32-0) and a finish platform past it (finish box x 4450-4850, y 0-800). Walking into the first spring: momentum (4800, 175), Velocity (0, 630) and the spring cutscene (0.25 s stick lock). A spring dash (the step's springDash 1, lockX 1: a dash pressed on the lock's first tick, which cancels the cutscene, 1236-1243) right moves momentum into preDashMomentum (1643-1644) and holds the dot level at 33.4 u a tick; the second spring's hit calls endDash first (hitSpring 2436-2439), which gives back 95% of preDashMomentum.x (sign matches the dash, dashDirection.y 0: 2030-2033), then adds its own 4800: momentum.x 9255 on tick 26. Without the dash the launch rises (Velocity.y 630) over the second spring's trigger, keeps one spring's momentum and comes down on the strip.
